source.title: Any-stepsize Gradient Descent for Separable Data under Fenchel-Young Losses
source.authors: Han Bao; Shinsaku Sakaue; Yuki Takezawa

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests and qualifies the broad training-convergence claim by proving arbitrary-stepsize convergence for separable linear classifiers under specified Fenchel–Young losses, and explicitly limits a direct extension to deep homogeneous networks as a future direction.
record.gate_note: The study's own results are theory for linear classifiers on bounded, linearly separable data, plus a toy four-point pilot study. It does not report CIFAR benchmarks, deep networks, random initialization, or training classification-error measurements. The paper notes that extending the setup to deep homogeneous networks is deferred. Theorem statements and rates are recorded as results; cited findings about neural networks and Wu et al. are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence for separable linear classifiers and illustrates it on four points. None of its own results tests V1–V6. Its connection to V5 is motivational: it does not establish neural-network curvature dynamics, recovery above an initial stability threshold, or divergence at larger rates.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the main theorem guarantees an iterate with arbitrarily small empirical risk under its separability and loss assumptions, rather than last-iterate or monotone convergence. Self-bounding is unnecessary for this guarantee, and separation margin improves sufficient rates in several examples. Deep-network extensions remain outside the study.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes GD on linear classifiers with Fenchel–Young losses and separable data, rather than the claim's large non-convex networks trained from random initialization. Its main evidence is theoretical; the pilot experiment uses a four-point toy dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: The guaranteed rate depends on the loss potential and whether it has separation margin; the paper gives distinct rates by entropy family and parameter q. In the pilot study, loss curves are shown across loss choices and stepsizes.

fits_no_version.finding: For bounded separable linear classification, the study proves best-iterate risk guarantees for arbitrary fixed positive GD stepsizes under specified Fenchel–Young losses. Separation margin yields faster sufficient bounds for several losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GD from zero initialization can attain arbitrarily small empirical risk on bounded linearly separable binary data under specified Fenchel–Young losses, with sufficient iteration bounds depending on the loss.

fits_no_version.finding: The four-point pilot and accompanying prose report finite-time zero loss for Tsallis 1.5 and 2 at sufficiently large stepsizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some Fenchel–Young losses with separation margin attain exact zero loss in finite time on the reported separable linear toy problem.

record.problems: The main findings are theoretical guarantees for linear models under bounded separability assumptions, not empirical deep-network or benchmark results. The authors explicitly defer extension to deep homogeneous networks. The pilot study is a four-point toy dataset and its trajectories are figure-only; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: R11 is cited prior-work recap, not a result produced by this study, so it is not retained as a catalog row. Figure 2 reports parameter-norm trajectories, but they do not measure the behavior named in any claim version and are omitted.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional networks, CIFAR datasets, corrupted labels, random initialization, capacity and recipe comparisons, and training classification error.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and extra-width comparisons.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, initialization-dependent training speed, and trainable depth.
All parts: squared-loss wide networks, initial linearized stability thresholds, loss-rise and curvature-drop recovery, sharpness hovering, and divergence.
All parts: batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Deferring deep networks does not qualify or challenge the neural-network versions. Section 5 mistakenly describes Tsallis 1.5 and 2 as lacking separation margin; Section 4 explicitly establishes that they have it. The omitted SGD extension also concerns separable linear classification and adds no evidence for V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training classification error.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and width comparisons.
Depth, batch-normalized or residual convolutional networks, and shortcut or normalization comparisons.
Initialization choices and their effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Stability limits, loss curvature dynamics, and recovery or divergence at above-threshold learning rates in neural networks.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training results.

rows.subject: linear classifier w
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 5: gradient descent with fixed stepsize from w0=0 on bounded linearly separable data under a Fenchel–Young loss satisfying Assumption 3.

conditions.value: Fenchel–Young loss satisfying Assumption 3; α, Cϕ ∈ (0, ∞)

rows.value: If T > (n/Cϕγ²)·4ρ(γ²ηT)/η + Cg ε−α, then mint∈[T] L(wt) ≤ ε.
rows.note: The result concerns convex linear classification under stated assumptions. The conclusion is a minimum risk over the trajectory, not a neural-network training classification-error result.
rows.check: No claim version applies. Correct the bound to T > [n/(Cϕγ²)]·[4√ρ(γ²ηT)/η + Cg]·ε^(−α); the recorded expression loses the square root and misplaces factors.

rows.check: No claim version applies. Correct the bound to T > [n/(Cϕγ²)]·[4m/η + Cg]·ε^(−α).

rows.subject: linear classifier w under logistic loss
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 5 rate instantiation for GD under the Shannon entropy potential, which generates logistic loss.
rows.baseline: stable-regime classical rate, stated as T = Ω(ε−1)
rows.value: T ≳ [4√2(log2(γ²η)+1)/η] + [4√2 n ε−1/(γ²η)], with logarithmic factors in ε−1 ignored.
rows.note: The authors characterize this as recovering the standard GD convergence rate under the stable regime with arbitrary stepsize.
rows.check: No claim version applies. The recorded explicit bound misplaces factors. Appendix F.1 gives, ignoring logarithmic factors, T ≳ [4√2·log₂(γ²η)/η + 1/ln 2 + 4√2/η]·nε^(−1)/γ².

rows.subject: linear classifier w under semi-circle loss
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 5 rate instantiation for GD using the semi-circle entropy potential.
rows.baseline: T = Ω(ε−1) for general convex smooth functions (as stated by the authors)
rows.value: T = Ω(ε−4) for arbitrary stepsize; η = Ω(ε−2) improves the rate to T = Ω(ε−2).
rows.note: The text says the arbitrary-stepsize rate is worse than the general convex smooth-function rate and attributes this to the perceptron argument being merely sufficient.
rows.check: No claim version applies. Preserve logarithmic suppression for the improved rate: the text states T = Ω̃(ε^(−2)). These are sufficient guarantees, not measured training speeds or lower bounds on required iterations.
